title: Copper had no source inside the walls, so the graph stopped at depth 2. It now reaches 5 — in a scenario that says out loud why it is not the reference run

verified.the hole, named: copper_ore was a RAW material with exactly one source, a drill on a copper field. Measured on seed 7 by probing a 3x3 drill site over a 90x90 window (tmp/f5/seams.gd): nearest copper 37 tiles SE at (165,165); nearest iron 34 tiles E at (161,132); coal at (124,95) north. copper_coil feeds pipe_segment and circuit, heat_core needs both, a warmth_radiator costs coil — so FOUR of the fourteen shipped recipes were unenterable without an expedition no scenario had ever mounted.
verified.the fix: game/content/recipes/salvaged_wire.tres — 8 scrap -> 2 copper_ore in a rubble sorter, 250 ticks, 0.16 ore/s against a drill's 0.80. Five sorters to one copper smelter, deliberately, so the copper field stays worth thirty tiles of pipe. Authoring source added to tests/production/author_content.gd. max_depth unchanged at 5.
verified.verified by deletion: with game/content/recipes/salvaged_wire.tres removed, 7 of the 9 go red — the reachable closure from rubble+coal loses copper_coil, pipe_segment, circuit and heat_core; set_recipe refuses the sorter; the live six-machine chain makes no coil. The 2 that stay green are the control (max_depth still 5) and the slag loop, which is what they are for.
verified.tests/scenarios/deep_chain.json (new) —: 5. The top of the shipped graph, reached for the first time in this project.

not_verified: tools/check.sh was not run end to end. Determinism, the production suites and assert_run against three runs were run individually.
No visual run and no perf measurement. Four cores shared with other agents all wave; perf numbers taken here would be noise and the integrator owns them.
deep_chain's own determinism replay was started but is a 2 x 43200-tick job; see the report.
open: [P05] citizens — THE BLOCKER, AND IT IS THE REASON first_night IS UNCHANGED. Machines finished after day one are assigned NOBODY. artifacts/F5_v2/state.json, citizens.staffing: buildings 354 (smelter), 355 (workshop), 356 (rubble_sorter) all read assigned:0, present:0, while the city held 44 citizens, 33 employed, 66 job slots and 42 required. Eleven idle people, nine unfilled slots. Until this lands a factory in the reference run is decoration. When it lands: re-run first_night with `_foundry_spine` / `_foundry` / `_retool` re-enabled in tools/gen_scenarios.py (they are written and tested, just not called from first_night) and raise the first_night production.chain_depth band from 2 to 4.

[P06] society / [P05] citizens — THE REFERENCE CITY IS EXILED AT t25400, which is 1400 ticks after first_night stops measuring it. Discontent reaches 100 by day three in first_night as it stands, and the run only looks like a survival because it ends first. deep_chain buys eleven more in-game hours by signing named_graves, care_house and night_curfew and switching the night off entirely, and still falls at t47860. The named grievance is corpses. This is the single largest thing standing between this build and a long session.

[P02] heat — the reference city has no heat headroom at all for industry. Nine machines added 700 units of demand against a delivery that never passed 283, and [P02] sheds by priority so the entire factory went to power 0.00 and 25 buildings froze. Three burners alone fixed the heat (deficit peak 213 -> 100, hope floor 27.9 -> 46.9) and broke the belt: three more porter-fed bunkers pulled the haulers off the line (fuel_by_machine 1078 -> 507, fuel_by_porter 1201 -> 2067) and the south smelter, competing for the same coal, made 0 plates against 23. Adding supply to this layout is not free and the cost lands in [P03].

[P04]/[P02] interlock — `pipe_segment` costs 50 heat over 5 s against a workshop's 10 u/s rating, so it is the ONE recipe in the game that needs full power to turn at all. That is a good design property and a sharp cliff; a district that runs it needs its own burner and nothing in the UI says so.

[P07]/[P08] — `threat peace on` does not stop everything: deep_chain has peace set at tick 6 and still lost 47 structures to ash_spitters, pale_stalkers and the_long_cold across days 3-5. Either peace is spawn-only by design, in which case a scenario cannot switch the night off, or it leaks.

PRE-EXISTING REDS I DID NOT CAUSE, all measured on an untouched first_night (artifacts/F5_base, generated before any change of mine): combat.structures_lost final 3 vs band 2; heat.frozen_buildings final 1 vs band 0; logistics.lines_dry high 1 vs band 0; production.stalled final 7 vs band 6; and 'every wave ends' — the run ends with 9 enemies alive. tests/production/test_a_great_frost_slows_the_factory_down also fails on the pristine tree. Five gate bands and one production test were already red before this wave's work started.

production.stalled final_max 6 on first_night is now red at 7 and I did NOT move it. At tick 24000 the reference city is in the third night with every crew asleep, so all seven machines read `unstaffed`. Moving the threshold would have hidden exactly the finding above.

[P18] build_menu — game/content/buildings already gates inserter_mk2/splitter_mk2 on `circuit`, belt_mk3/underground_mk3 on `steel_plate`, heat_pipe_insulated on `insulation_wool` and geothermal_tap on `pipe_segment`. deep_chain now MAKES four of those five. Nothing in the UI tells a player that a tier opened a menu row; that is the cheapest 'progression you can feel' left on the table.

game/content/recipes/ammo_shell.tres is a dead letter: it needs sulfur, and there is no sulfur deposit within 44 tiles of the core on seed 7. Nothing in game/ consumes ammo_shell either. The munitions branch is decoration until [P07] spends it or the map places sulfur.
